entities.summary:
Charles de Lannoy (c. 1487 – 1527), a prominent soldier and statesman from the Low Countries, served as a key military commander and diplomat under the Habsburg emperors Maximilian I and Charles V during the pivotal Italian Wars (1494-1559). His career culminated as Viceroy of Naples, where he governed from 1522 until his death, playing a crucial role in consolidating Habsburg power in Italy and shaping the early modern European political landscape. He is best known for his decisive victory at the Battle of Pavia in 1525, which saw the capture of King Francis I of France, profoundly shifting the balance of power between France and the burgeoning Habsburg empire.

Lannoy's military prowess first came to prominence in the service of Maximilian I, participating in campaigns that solidified Habsburg influence. However, it was under Charles V that his career truly flourished. As commander of the imperial forces in Italy, Lannoy confronted the French armies led by King Francis I. The climactic engagement occurred on February 24, 1525, outside Pavia, where Lannoy's tactical brilliance, combining arquebusiers with pike formations and a well-timed cavalry charge, annihilated the French forces. This victory led directly to the capture of the French monarch, a diplomatic coup that allowed Charles V to dictate the terms of the Treaty of Madrid (1526).
